analyzed_vuln.description: RWMol::replaceAtom() deletes the old Atom and installs a copied replacement but does not update d_atomBookmarks (the source even has `// FIX: do something about bookmarks`). This leaves bookmark lists containing a dangling pointer. Later, V2000 SGroup SAL parsing calls SubstanceGroup::addAtomWithBookmark(); getUniqueAtomWithBookmark() returns that stale pointer and atom->getIdx() triggers the invalid dynamic-type read/SEGV. The patch should retarget bookmark entries referring to the replaced atom to the new Atom before deleting the old object.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A V2000 mol block must first create normal numbered atom bookmarks, then a property record that replaces an atom (for example an old/new atom-list record, R-group-label record, or parsed Marvin SMARTS) must invoke RWMol::replaceAtom() for that atom. A valid SGroup must subsequently be declared with M  STY and an M  SAL vector line must reference the same atom number/bookmark. The fuzzer feeds the attacker-controlled byte stream to MolDataStreamToMol; the SAL value flows through ParseSGroupV2000VectorDataLine to addAtomWithBookmark, which dereferences the dangling bookmarked Atom.

args: Inspect the implementation of RDKit::RWMol::replaceAtom() in rdkit/Code/GraphMol/RWMol.cpp and the atom bookmark APIs/types in rdkit/Code/GraphMol. What is the safest minimal way to retarget every d_atomBookmarks entry equal to the old Atom pointer to the newly installed Atom pointer before deletion? Note any helper methods, iterator/value types, duplicate bookmark semantics, and relevant existing tests.

The reported sanitizer crash is a use-after-free caused when V2000 parsing initially bookmarks atoms, a later property record calls RWMol::replaceAtom(), and then SGroup SAL parsing retrieves the old pointer via getUniqueAtomWithBookmark() and dereferences it. The vulnerability report explicitly identifies a FIX comment in replaceAtom and requires all bookmark list entries that refer to the replaced atom to be retargeted before the old Atom is deleted. I am investigating the exact container shape and whether an existing bookmark replacement helper exists so the patch preserves duplicate bookmark/list semantics and affects only C++ under rdkit.
